title: JANUS Genesis Sovereign v6.1 — Durable Hash Journal, Same-Host Fencing, Provider Idempotency Binding, and Deadline-Bounded Fairness
problem: v6.0 made cancellation, ambiguous dispatch, recovery, sagas, compensation, and anti-starvation explicit, but most control state still lived in process memory. A process crash could therefore forget cancellation/recovery/saga facts, and thread locks alone could not fence two processes sharing one effect key. v6.1 adds an fsync-backed append-only hash journal, deterministic replay projection, SQLite generation fencing for processes sharing one local database, explicit provider-idempotency contracts, and a deadline-aware fairness queue that preserves bounded access under urgent traffic.

durable_hash_journal.serialization: UTF-8 canonical JSON with sorted keys and compact separators
durable_hash_journal.integrity: event_hash = SHA256(canonical(sequence,event_type,payload,prev_hash)); replay rejects sequence gaps/reordering, prev-hash mismatch, schema mismatch, invalid JSON, or event-hash mismatch
durable_hash_journal.claim_limit: Hash chaining is tamper-evident, not an availability guarantee, remote replication guarantee, or protection against complete file deletion. fsync durability remains bounded by filesystem/platform behavior.

same_host_fencing.rule: Only the current holder/generation with an unexpired HELD lease validates.
same_host_fencing.takeover_rule: After expiry or release, a new holder receives generation+1; all older tokens become stale.
same_host_fencing.race_property: Two processes sharing the same SQLite file cannot both acquire the same unexpired effect fence through the tested transaction path.
same_host_fencing.scope_limit: This is a same-host/shared-filesystem coordination primitive. It is not a multi-host consensus algorithm and does not claim correctness over independent databases.

provider_idempotency_contract.principle: JANUS must not assume that a provider supports idempotency merely because retries are desirable.
provider_idempotency_contract.binding_rule: When idempotency is declared, provider key is derived from provider_id + namespace + protected effect_key, not from one authorization ID. Replacement authorizations for the same effect therefore reuse the same provider key.
provider_idempotency_contract.important_limit: The adapter contract is a declaration consumed by JANUS. Provider behavior and receipt authenticity still require provider-specific verification outside this generic module.

sequence: external executor acts outside this module
journaled_fenced_dispatch_intent.semantic_rule: Returning DurableDispatchIntent proves only that the control-plane intent is journaled and fenced; it is not a world receipt and does not prove external execution.

deadline_bounded_fairness.problem: Pure bounded-bypass fairness can ignore urgent deadlines, while pure earliest-deadline scheduling can starve ordinary dissent under an endless stream of overdue work.
mechanism: overdue tickets may preempt ordinary routing
risk rank and routing priority order overdue/ordinary peers
bypass_count still accumulates on nonselected tickets
after max_deadline_burst consecutive overdue selections, any mandatory max-bypass ticket must be served before another overdue burst continues
deadline_bounded_fairness.learning_relation: Risk/deadline/routing influence attention scheduling only; they do not authorize world effects or certify truth.

verified_cases.case: Cancellation -> NO_EFFECT reconciliation -> recovery authorization is journaled; a new journal instance replays the chain and reconstructs RECOVERY_AUTHORIZED state.
A previously journaled saga state is edited on disk without recomputing the chain.
PROCESS_B tries to acquire an unexpired effect fence held by PROCESS_A.
PROCESS_B takes over after lease expiry and receives a newer generation; PROCESS_A reuses old token.
Original and replacement authorizations target the same effect at an idempotent provider.
An old low-priority ticket becomes mandatory while new overdue critical tickets keep arriving.

new_open_edges.name: DEFAULT_EXECUTOR_ADAPTER_INTEGRATION
new_open_edges.risk: The durable/fenced control plane is additive; mature Genesis external execution paths are not yet forced through it.
new_open_edges.next_requirement: explicit adapter contract and shadow/enforced integration gate

new_open_edges.name: CRASH_INJECTION_AT_EVERY_BOUNDARY
new_open_edges.risk: Unit tests replay completed writes but do not yet inject process death before/after every fsync, fence acquisition, validation, receipt append, and fence release boundary.
new_open_edges.next_requirement: deterministic crash matrix with restart assertions

new_open_edges.name: PROVIDER_RECEIPT_VERIFICATION
new_open_edges.risk: Generic structural binding does not authenticate provider receipts.
new_open_edges.next_requirement: provider-specific verifier interface and signed/lookup-backed receipt tests

new_open_edges.name: MULTI_HOST_BACKEND
new_open_edges.risk: SQLite fencing is not a distributed consensus backend.
new_open_edges.next_requirement: optional external strongly consistent lease/CAS backend with fencing-token semantics
